messages:
miguel: Heads-up — we have the Q3 large-batch inference run next Tue. Our cost target is -18% vs last run but we can’t let p95 latency jump >10%. Thinking about a different procurement mix: capacity-optimized pools for steady state + opportunistic low-price pools for burst, with a small cross-region warm buffer and fast eviction handling. Thoughts?

sana: +1 to mixing. key thing is failover latency when a price pool evaporates. warm buffer needs to be cross-AZ (not just regional) so routing doesn't add minutes. 10% warm buffer? maybe 8-12%.

jordan: agree on buffer. also we should prefer capacity-optimized in regions with historically high spot churn. price-optimized in low-churn markets. do we have churn metrics by instance type/region?

miguel: yes — attached short stats (summary): eu-west-1 for A100-like preemptibles has 6% hourly eviction vs 18% in us-east-1 for cheaper mixes. so use capacity-optimized in us-east-1, price-optimized in eu-west-1 and ap-south-1.

leah: operational note: mixing pools means we need deterministic placement for long-running jobs so they avoid tailing off on eviction. Suggest: prefer capacity-optimized for long jobs, price-optimized only for short batch shards or retryable shards.

raj: propose runtime rules:
```
pool_rules:
  - job_type: long-running
    prefer: capacity-optimized
  - job_type: short-shard
    allow: price-optimized
warmbuffer:
  size_pct: 10
  ttl_seconds: 900
failover:
  spill_policy: immediate
  max_retries: 2
```

raj: also, set preemptible-drain-handler to immediately checkpoint + resubmit to fallback pool. checkpointing should be <30s.

sana: + :thumbsup: on checkpoint <30s. We should instrument cost attribution per-shard so we can see unit cost delta between pools (tokens/sec per dollar).

miguel: quick simulation I ran locally: replacing 25% of baseline with price-optimized bursts saved ~21% cost but increased p95 by 6% in a bad region. With 10% warmbuffer and 2x spill capacity in capacity-optimized pools, p95 delta dropped to 2%.

ops-bot: deploy-log: created warmbuffer group "wb-q3-batch" (size=10% across eu-west-1/us-east-1), attached to cluster inference-prod-2.

jordan: nit: ensure we don’t mix instance series in same warmbuffer group (mixing A100/RTX may cause kernel mismatch and waste). keep buffer homogeneous.

leah: action items:
- raj: draft the pool_rules and drain-handler config (ETA: EOD)
- sana: add churn-by-region dashboard + cost-per-shard chart (ETA: tomorrow)
- miguel: run 1 low-risk canary with 5% price-optimized on weds (ETA: Weds morning)

miguel: thanks folks. If canary looks good we ramp to 25% for the main run, but keep automatic rollback threshold at p95 +10% and cost savings >15%.

ops-bot: alert: if warmbuffer falls below 70% of target, will trigger auto-topup to maintain cross-region buffer.

sana: one more thought — include soft-eviction window: when price-optimized nodes see market signal, mark slots as "do-not-schedule-long-jobs" for 60s to reduce mid-exec preempts.

miguel: good call. add to rules: soft-eviction=60s.

leah: I'll own the post-mortem template for the run (cost/latency/regional-behavior).

miguel: closing: final config should be committed to infra repo under `infra/procurement/q3-batch.yaml` and a short runbook in runbooks/q3-batch.md.
